# ui::Accessibility

Header: `winui/ui/Accessibility.hpp`.

The semantic name and description a control exposes to assistive technology ([`name`](#name) / [`description`](#description)).

Every spec carries an `.accessibility` field and every [Element](element.md) stores one ([Element::accessibility()](element.md#accessibility) / [Element::set_accessibility()](element.md#set_accessibility)). A control with a visible label derives its accessible name from that label, so [`ui::Button{.text = "Save"}`](../controls/button.md#uibutton) needs nothing. Only content with no readable text of its own, such as an icon-only button, a progress ring or a bare image, has to say what it is.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::Button{.width         = 50.0f,
                   .height        = 50.0f,
                   .accessibility = {.name        = "Save document",
                                     .description = "Saves the current document"},
                   .on_click      = [] { /* save */ },
                   .content       = ui::Icon{.source = ui::Symbol::Save}},
        ui::ProgressRing{.active = true, .accessibility = {.name = "Saving"}},
    },
});

// Imperative path: the same value on the retained control.
auto divider = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("|");
divider->set_accessibility({.decorative = true});
```

## name

```cpp
std::string name {}
```

The short name announced for this control ("Save document"). Empty derives the name from the control's own visible text, which is right for almost every control.

## description

```cpp
std::string description {}
```

A longer explanation, announced after the name when a screen reader asks for it. Usually empty. Add one only when the name is not enough.

## decorative

```cpp
bool decorative = false
```

True when this control tells a screen reader nothing its neighbors don't already say, such as a decorative icon beside a label that repeats it, a separator or a spacer. Screen readers then skip it, so it isn't announced twice.

## automation_id

```cpp
std::string automation_id {}
```

A fixed identifier that UI test tools find this control by ("save-button"). It stays the same from run to run and across languages, while the name changes with the text. Empty reports none. Screen readers don't read it.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True when nothing was specified, so the control falls back to its visible text.
